 Blood pressure medication recalled nationwide over possible metal contamination 
 Anyone who was prescribed the drug from the impacted lot was advised to "immediately" stop taking it and contact their doctor. 
 Published November 16, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 16, 2026 at 12:37 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 Recalls occur when manufacturers and distributors remove products “that present a risk of injury or gross deception or are otherwise defective,” according to the FDA.
 Check your medicine cabinets: A new nationwide recall has been issued for some pills typically used to treat high blood pressure because they may be contaminated with metal. 
 Breckenridge Pharmaceutical, Inc. issued the voluntary recall Monday for one lot of Propranolol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules. The 60 mg white capsules are manufactured by Adare Pharma and could potentially contain pieces of metal.

   WATCH HERE 
 The pills could potentially cause "lacerations of soft tissues in the oral cavity, esophagus, stomach, or intestine," the announcement said. To date, the company said it was not aware of any adverse health events related to the recall. 
 The affected capsules were distributed nationwide to wholesalers and pharmacies between Oct. 26, 2026 and Nov., 04, 2026, the announcement said. 
 According to the Cleveland Clinic , propranolol extended-release capsules are beta-blockers that lower blood pressure and heart rate, and are typically are used to treat hypertension.

 "Consumers should return any unused portion of the affected product to the pharmacy where it was obtained," the announcement said. 
 The pharmaceutical company also asked that wholesalers, pharmacies and retailers check their inventory for the affected lot. 
 The recall is the latest in a series of recent blood pressure medication recalls, including one earlier this month involving Olmesartan Medoxomil, Amlodipine and Hydrochlorothiazide tablets, which were recalled because they did not dissolve properly .
 Earlier this fall, thousands of bottles of Chlorthalidone tablets were recalled for the same reason. 
 Breckenridge Pharmaceutical Inc. did not immediately respond to NBC Chicago's request for comment.
